title: Steam Locomotive: Stephenson's Rocket
body:
Steam Locomotive: Stephenson's Rocket was built in 1829 and won the Rainhill Trials, proving that steam locomotives could carry passengers reliably and quickly. Rocket's design — a multi-tube boiler, a blast pipe, and a direct drive — set the pattern for steam locomotives for a century.

Stephenson's Rocket is a public fact of railway history, and its success launched the railway age.

title: High-Speed Train: Shinkansen
body:
High-Speed Train: Shinkansen is Japan's bullet train, which entered service in 1964 between Tokyo and Osaka and proved that dedicated high-speed rail could carry millions safely. Shinkansen trains run at up to 320 kilometres per hour on their own lines, with a safety record unmatched in transport.

The Shinkansen changed what a train could be, and its success inspired high-speed rail on every continent.

title: Diesel Locomotive
body:
Diesel Locomotive is a locomotive powered by a diesel engine driving electric traction motors, the standard freight and passenger locomotive in much of the world after steam. Diesel locomotives are rugged, long-ranged, and able to work lines without electrification.

Diesel locomotives replaced steam across the twentieth century, and their sound is the sound of freight rail.

title: Electric Multiple Unit
body:
Electric Multiple Unit is a passenger train whose cars each carry their own traction motors, fed from overhead wires or a third rail, giving fast acceleration and frequent stops. Electric multiple units dominate commuter and regional services in electrified countries.

Electric multiple units are the work horses of city and regional rail, quiet, clean at the point of use, and quick off the mark.

title: Freight Train
body:
Freight Train is a train of wagons carrying containers, coal, grain, cars, or bulk goods over long distances. Freight trains are the most energy-efficient way to move heavy goods on land, and a single train can carry the load of hundreds of trucks.

Freight trains are the arteries of continental economies, and their long consists are a familiar sight on prairie and desert lines.

title: Metro Train
body:
Metro Train is a train built for urban rapid transit, running frequently through tunnels and on elevated lines with high capacity and fast boarding. Metro trains carry millions of city dwellers daily, and their design is about throughput: wide doors, standing room, and rapid acceleration.

Metro trains make dense cities work, and their networks are the skeleton of urban life.

title: Tram
body:
Tram is a light rail vehicle running on street tracks, sharing roads with traffic in city centres and running on reserved tracks in suburbs. Trams combine the capacity of a train with the street access of a bus, and they have returned to many cities after a mid-century decline.

Trams are the friendly face of rail, and their bells and street running are part of city identity.

title: Maglev Train
body:
Maglev Train is a train that floats on magnetic levitation, with no wheels touching a rail, and is propelled by linear motors. The Shanghai Maglev, opened in 2004, runs at up to 431 kilometres per hour, the fastest commercial train service in the world.

Maglev trains are a glimpse of rail's future, where friction itself is engineered away.
